opening: I have ten minutes. Ask me what you need, and I will tell you what I actually want.
unknownReply: I have not decided that. What would you suggest, and what would it cost me?
refusal: I am the customer, not the author. I can tell you what I need; the wording is your job.

facts.answer: It is for the person who opens TaskTrackr first thing in the morning and wants to know what they have already missed, before they plan the day.

facts.topic: whether a task due today is overdue
facts.answer: A task due today is not overdue. It is late tomorrow morning, not this morning.
If I finished it, I do not want to see it, even if I finished it late. The report is a list of things still owed.

facts.topic: what order the report is in
facts.answer: Most overdue first. If two are equally late, the higher priority one goes on top.
A task with no due date is never overdue. I use the date field when I mean it.
No reminders, no emails, no notifications. I will look at the report when I want it.

facts.topic: what an empty report should say
facts.answer: If nothing is overdue, say so in a sentence. An empty list with no words looks like a bug.
I want it as its own page, not a filter on the list. I open it once in the morning and then I go away.

facts.topic: what a row of the report shows
facts.answer: The title, how late it is in days, and the list it came from. If I have to click through to find out which list, it is not a report.

facts.topic: whether it is a new screen or a new endpoint
facts.answer: That is your problem. I want one place to look.
